title: SuperAudio Device Profile
description: Schema v1 — describes how to talk to one audio device model (sink role) and how to observe its state (control role). MIT-licensed pure data, no executable content.

schemaVersion.description: Schema version. Bumped only on breaking changes. Old consumers ignore unknown fields; new optional fields land additively without bumping this.

id.description: Stable identifier for this device profile. Convention: '<manufacturer-slug>-<model-slug>'. Used as the filename + as a join key for telemetry-free contributors-style sharing.

displayName.description: Human-readable name shown in UI. e.g., 'Bowers & Wilkins A5'.

firstRelease.description: Year the device first shipped, if known. Helps prioritise legacy-device profiles.

lastFirmware.description: Most recent firmware version this profile has been verified against, if known.

match.description: How the SuperAudio discovery layer recognises this device. Order of fields = order of confidence; first match wins.

bonjourServiceType.description: Bonjour/mDNS service type. e.g., '_raop._tcp' for AirPlay 1, '_sonos._tcp' for Sonos.

modelHints.description: Substrings to look for in the device's mDNS TXT record or HTTP description. e.g., ['B&W', 'BW-A5']. Case-insensitive substring match.

macOUI.description: Optional list of MAC OUI prefixes for the manufacturer. Tiebreaker only — never the primary match because some devices share OUIs across product lines.

roles.description: Roles this device can play in a SuperAudio session. At least one of sink/control must be non-null.

sink.description: How to send audio TO this device. Null if the device is control-only (e.g., a soundbar paired with an Audio Bridge).

control.description: How to observe volume/power/state events FROM this device. Null if the device is sink-only or doesn't expose events.

verifiedBy.description: Names or GitHub handles of contributors who verified this profile on real hardware. Empty array if seeded from public references only.

verifiedDate.description: ISO 8601 date of last hardware verification, or null if never verified on physical hardware.

contributedDate.description: ISO 8601 date this profile was first contributed.

notes.description: Free-text notes for downstream consumers. Plain English. The most useful thing to fill in for legacy devices.

protocol.description: Protocol family used to send audio to this sink. Determines which SuperAudio module handles the session.

compressed.description: False = raw PCM in container. True = compressed codec. Important for ALAC where escape=1 (verbatim) vs compressed behaves differently across receivers.

container.description: If applicable: 'adts' for AAC over HTTP, 'm4a' for AAC in MP4 fragment, etc.

et.description: AirPlay 1 encryption type: 0 = unencrypted, 1 = RSA-OAEP-SHA1 with Apple AirPort Express public key. Some receivers require et=1 even though et=0 is sufficient on others.

fallback.description: If primary encryption fails, what to try next. e.g., 'et=1' if et=0 fails.

audioLatencyMs.description: Receiver-side buffer depth in milliseconds (the value the receiver advertises in its RECORD response's Audio-Latency header for AirPlay 1, or measured empirically for other protocols). For Sonos, this is the OBSERVABLE renderer-to-DAC delay; for AirPlay 1, the negotiated value.

buffer.description: Free-text description of how this sink buffers audio. e.g., 'RTP timestamp-based, ~93ms', 'Renderer buffer 0.5-4 sec variable, NOT exposed via API'.

transport.description: Protocol-specific transport hints (e.g., Sonos's URI scheme requirements).

quirks.description: Free-text list of known firmware quirks. The most valuable field for downstream consumers debugging a 'why does this device behave weirdly' issue.

muted.description: Special value indicating muted (e.g., -144 for AirPlay 1 dB scale).

knownFirmware.description: Firmware versions this profile has been observed working with, if known.

controlRole.description: How to observe events FROM this device. Used when a device is the 'audio brain' of a room (typically a soundbar) and the rest of the mesh needs to follow its volume/power/source state.

subscriptionEndpoint.description: URL path or service identifier for the event subscription endpoint. e.g., '/MediaRenderer/RenderingControl/Event' for Sonos UPnP eventing.

irCodesLearned.description: True if this device requires IR-remote-learning to capture power/source events. False if events come over a network protocol.

fallbackStrategy.description: Free-text description of what to do when no event path works. e.g., 'Poll volume every 5 sec via UPnP query'.
